name: PhD Program
author: Jump Science (Coach Daniel Back)
summary: For athletes who are decently strong and already jump well. Builds max strength, then shifts back toward explosive and elastic ability.

swaps.details: single reps, light building to heavy; go heavy enough to feel how strong you are

guidelines: The training is organized into up to 4 workouts per week. They should be scheduled to give you a day of rest before the first three workouts (example: MWF for three workouts or MWFSat for four)
There is also a stretching routine and a series of therapeutic isometrics. These tools are both meant to be used as needed. More info is on the next two pages.
Weight recommendations are light, medium, heavy, or a percentage.
Light weight = 5 out of 10 or lower difficulty. Medium = 6-8 out of 10, no struggling to finish the set. Heavy = 9-10 out of 10, the last rep is difficult to complete.
When the weight is a percentage such as (60%) this refers to your max deep squat. ALL THE PERCENTAGES IN THE PROGRAM REFER TO MAX DEEP SQUAT.
In the "sets x reps (weight)" column, 4x5 (medium) means 4 sets of 5 reps with medium weight.
When more than one weight is listed such as 4x5 (60, 70, 80, 90%) or (50% to heavy) do the first set with the light weight and build up to the heaviest weight for the final set.
Rest as needed between sets and between exercises. This may mean resting 30 seconds between sets of easy hops or resting 5 minutes after a hard set of squats. Use your judgement.
Even if you are familiar with an exercise, please watch the instructional video. Details of exercise execution are important.
Please pay attention to the details column.

weeks.decision:
If you have been getting stronger and more athletic over the last 6 weeks, you do not need to interrupt that process. Go back to week 5 and keep the gains rolling.

If you have been getting stronger but your jumping ability is lagging behind, move on to the explosive shift phase in weeks 11-16. The reduction in strength training and overall easier schedule should help athletic gains show up.

If you have not been getting stronger or jumping higher, take a couple easy weeks similar to week 10 but without the max squat. This should help your body get fresh. Examine your nutrition, sleep, stress, and sports schedule to try to figure out why you were not getting stronger. When you're ready you can restart the program at week 1.

weeks.decision:
After the last six weeks, most athletes are probably in a good spot to start strength training again. However if you have jumped progressively higher throughout the explosive shift phase, you have the option to repeat some or all of weeks 11-16 to see if there are still gains to be had from minimizing strength training.

If your jumping has been stagnant or has decreased in the last 6 weeks, your body still has had a chance to shift explosively and get fresh. You should be ready to benefit from strength training again. Re- start the program and expect good things.

Regardless of results, you also have the option of taking some time away from training to completely rest up.
